comment: Identifies self-supervised CTG trajectory representation and calibrated neonatal risk enrichment in the target intrapartum CTG population.
Single-paragraph abstract aligned with Frontiers in Signal Processing biomedical signal-processing positioning.
Explains intrapartum CTG decision-support context and limitations of static or subjective interpretation.
Target population is intrapartum CTG records; intended use is risk enrichment and phenotype interpretation rather than autonomous diagnosis.
No protected sociodemographic fairness analysis was possible beyond available CTU-UHB metadata; this is treated as a limitation.
Objective is evaluation of an open-data self-supervised CTG trajectory-representation workflow for calibrated neonatal risk enrichment.
CTU-UHB/CTU-CHB is primary raw-signal cohort; CTGDL-FHRMA is external representation/domain-shift resource; UCI CTG is feature-level reference.
Public datasets are cited with access information; detailed original accrual dates depend on source metadata.
Intrapartum cardiotocography public data from hospital-based CTG resources.
Records included when raw FHR/UC and required metadata were available for the analysis pipeline.
No treatment-effect modelling was performed; delivery process variables were not used as intervention exposures.
Signal windowing, missingness, feature extraction, train-only scaling and source-data generation are described.
Primary endpoint is cord pH <7.15 or 5-minute Apgar <7 at record level.
Outcome uses recorded pH and Apgar metadata from the public dataset rather than new subjective adjudication.
Retrospective public-data analysis; outcome labels were withheld from SSL pretraining.
Classical signal features and SSL embeddings were prespecified from CTG physiology and self-supervised representation design.
Signal features, SSL embedding dimensions and phenotype variables are described; source-data tables are included.
Predictors were algorithmically extracted from public CTG signals and metadata.
Record counts, event counts and window counts are reported; limitations discuss small event count and high-dimensional model risk.
Median imputation, missingness features and no-missingness sensitivity are reported.
Record-level training/test split, train-only SSL pretraining and held-out validation are stated.
Numeric predictors were median-imputed and standardized; categorical phenotypes were one-hot encoded.
Transformer SSL, logistic pipelines, exploratory compact sweep and development-only selection sensitivity are described.
Domain-shift analysis compares CTU-UHB with CTGDL-FHRMA; formal multi-centre heterogeneity was not possible.
AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, calibration, decision curve and bootstrap CIs are reported with rationale.
Cross-fitted Platt and isotonic recalibration are described; Platt scaling is emphasized.
Pipeline scripts are named and the versioned repository archive is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20376424.
Class-balanced logistic regression and AUPRC emphasis are justified under event imbalance.
Available public metadata did not support a full fairness assessment; age and clinical stratification were limited.
Outputs are risk-enrichment scores and calibrated probabilities; not intended as definitive diagnosis.
CTU train/test split and CTGDL representation-domain differences are explicitly described.
Public de-identified datasets; ethics approval not applicable.
No specific funding.
No competing interests declared.
No formal protocol was registered; analysis scripts and source data are included for reproducibility.
Study was not registered.
Public data sources and derived source-data tables are listed.
Local scripts are identified; the GitHub repository and versioned Zenodo archive are reported in Code availability.
No patient or public involvement in this retrospective public-data analysis.
Cohort scale and train/test records are shown.
Dataset scale and available record-level characteristics are summarized in supplementary files.
Train/test event balance and external domain-shift analysis are reported.

topic: Number of participants and events per analysis
comment: Events are reported for primary and sensitivity analyses.
Architecture, feature dimensions and logistic models are described; implementation scripts are included in the GitHub repository and versioned Zenodo archive.
Performance estimates include bootstrap confidence intervals and model differences.
Domain-shift and missingness sensitivity are reported; subgroup fairness analysis remains limited.
Platt and isotonic recalibration results are reported.
Interprets risk enrichment, phenotype physiology, calibration and external-domain boundaries.
Discusses retrospective design, model-selection sensitivity, event count, dimensionality, missingness and lack of external outcome validation.

topic: Handling poor quality or unavailable inputs
comment: Missingness sensitivity and signal-quality features are reported; deployment handling is future work.
Model is positioned for clinician-facing decision support rather than autonomous use.
Calls for larger locked train/development/test designs, external outcome validation and prospective evaluation.
